headline: Going Commando reaches 7,100 matched functions on USA v1.01
summary: Contributors integrated a large batch of reconstructed C, taking USA v1.01 to 65.83% matched code by size and 7,100 of 8,578 functions. USA v2.00 ends at 6,646 of 8,634 matched functions, and PAL at 4,979 of 8,672. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game.
highlights: #368 carries over 842 functions from a contributor's fork: 158 boot and 684 level functions, covering 609,116 USA v1.01 code bytes. Its 73,572 additions and 59,161 deletions dominate the day's 105,041 additions and 68,398 deletions.
The earlier refresh in #367 records matched code at 54.81% for USA v1.01, 32.09% for USA v2.00 and 17.49% for PAL, before the large carry-over.
#364 adds 21 matches; #366 integrates reviewed contributor work while retaining a function with an initialization concern as a near miss.
Parallel builds now give each program its own Wine prefix, avoiding a shared single-threaded bottleneck. #369 fixes the accounting of fully linked code units.
Object-slot and held-object reconstructions in #370 and #371 remain open.
